settings.heading: The World's Most Accessible Bamboo Bike Frame
settings.subtitle: The bamboo bicycle frame grows on every continent except Europe and Antarctica — nearly 1,600 species. No factories, foundries, or billion-dollar supply chains. Anyone can build their own bamboo frame in two days.

settings.seo_title: Bamboo Bicycle Frame Testing at Swansea University
settings.seo_description: Bamboo Bicycle Club working with Swansea University to conduct three-point flexural bending tests on bamboo tubes used for bicycle frame construction, confirming high stiffness and engineering performance.

settings.heading: Stronger Than Steel, Gram for Gram
settings.text:
Bamboo's tensile strength reaches around 28,000 PSI — in the same range as mild steel, but at a fraction of the weight. Unlike steel, bamboo is a natural composite: parallel cellulose fibres in a lignin matrix, running the full length of the culm. The same structural principle as carbon fibre, evolved over millions of years.

We tested this with Swansea University. Their three-point flexural bending tests on our actual bamboo tubes confirmed high stiffness and consistent mechanical properties across samples. The results showed bamboo behaves like a high-performance engineering material — because it is one.

settings.heading: A Ride You Can Actually Feel
settings.text:
The fibre structure that makes bamboo strong also makes it comfortable. Those parallel fibres absorb road vibration naturally — something aluminium and steel simply can't match. Less buzz through the handlebars, less fatigue over long distances, a smoother ride on rough roads.

This isn't marketing. It's physics. Bamboo's natural damping properties have been documented in structural engineering for decades. In a bicycle frame, it means you arrive fresher, with less strain on your hands, wrists, and back.

settings.heading: Why It Matters
settings.text:
To make an aluminium frame, you need bauxite mines, smelters running at 1,000°C, and factories with CNC machines. Carbon fibre requires petroleum-derived precursors, autoclaves, and clean rooms.

To make a bamboo bicycle frame, you need bamboo, a jig, hand tools, and two days. That's it.

In Ghana, the Bamboo Bikes Initiative creates jobs and affordable transport using locally-grown bamboo. In London, we teach beginners — 95% with zero mechanical experience — to build their own bamboo frames in a weekend. In prisons, our Build to Bond programme uses frame-building to reconnect fathers with their children.

settings.heading: The Carbon Maths
settings.text:
A peer-reviewed lifecycle analysis by Wageningen University found that bamboo bicycle frames have approximately 50% lower environmental impact than aluminium frames, and about 30% less than steel.

Bamboo reaches structural maturity in 3–5 years. Trees take 20–50. It regenerates from its root system — no replanting needed. It doesn't require pesticides or irrigation. And it actively sequesters carbon as it grows.

Most carbon fibre sports equipment has just a 3-year lifespan — and 90% of it ends up in landfill (UCI). A bamboo frame? Still being ridden a decade later.

settings.heading: Ancient Material, Modern Engineering
settings.text:
Bamboo has been used structurally for thousands of years — bridges, scaffolding, entire buildings across Asia, South America, and Africa. The first bamboo bicycle was patented in England in 1894 by the Bamboo Cycle Company, and shown at the London Stanley Cycle Show the same year.

What's changed is the jointing. Modern connections using carbon fibre and epoxy resin create joints stronger than the bamboo itself. Combined with precision jigs and heat-treated tubes, the result is a frame that meets the demands of serious cyclists while remaining buildable by complete beginners.

Over 4,000 people in 36+ countries have built bamboo bicycle frames with us since 2012. Featured in the Financial Times, BikeRadar, and the Design Museum's Cycle Revolution exhibition.

settings.question: Does a bamboo bicycle frame crack or split?
settings.answer: Properly treated and sealed bamboo is very stable. Our tubes are heat-treated to remove moisture and sealed with epoxy resin. Store indoors and avoid prolonged exposure to extreme wet conditions.

settings.question: Can I ride a bamboo bike in the rain?
settings.answer: Yes. Finished bamboo bicycle frames are fully sealed with epoxy resin. Dry your bike after wet rides and store it indoors — the same care you'd give any quality frame.

settings.question: Is bamboo really stronger than steel?
settings.answer: Per unit weight, yes. Bamboo's tensile strength is around 28,000 PSI — in the same range as mild steel — but bamboo is significantly lighter, giving it a superior strength-to-weight ratio. This is confirmed by our Swansea University mechanical testing.

settings.question: What about the joints on a bamboo bicycle frame?
settings.answer: The joints are the strongest part. Carbon fibre and epoxy resin lugs exceed the strength of the bamboo tubes themselves. Our jointing method has been refined over 13 years and 4,000+ builds.

settings.question: How long will a bamboo bicycle frame last?
settings.answer: 8–12 years with proper care. Under 1% failure rate across 4,000+ frames. Many of our 2012 builds are still being ridden daily.

settings.question: Do I need experience to build a bamboo bike frame?
settings.answer: No. 95% of our builders have zero mechanical experience. Workshop frames are completed in 2 days with full expert guidance. Home kits include step-by-step instructions and video tutorials.

settings.question: What types of bamboo bicycle can I build?
settings.answer: Any type. Road, gravel, mountain, cargo, tandem, balance bike — we've seen them all. The geometry is defined by your jig setup, so the frame design is entirely up to you. Browse our build stories to see what's possible.

settings.question: Is bamboo a sustainable material for bicycles?
settings.answer: Yes — it's one of the most sustainable structural materials on the planet. A peer-reviewed lifecycle analysis by Wageningen University found bamboo bicycle frames have ~50% lower environmental impact than aluminium. Bamboo reaches structural maturity in 3–5 years, sequesters carbon as it grows, and requires no pesticides or irrigation.
